question_set_contract.dependency_contract: Exactly two questions use prior learning: q01 directly retrieves the previous hydrostatic-pressure lesson and q07 mixes that method with the current pressure-force explanation.
question_set_contract.difficulty_progression: direct prerequisite retrieval, three conceptual diagnostics, force-direction analysis, a two-stage calculation, then a mixed explanation and calculation with an unequal shape

evidence_basis.originality_note: All objects, wording, values, answer choices and figure briefs are original. The official evidence supplies only the assessed pressure-difference and resultant-force patterns.

questions.prompt: State the relationship for the hydrostatic pressure difference between two levels in a static fluid of uniform density, and identify the quantity that describes the separation of the levels.
A fluid touches a small horizontal patch on the top of a submerged object. In which direction is the force exerted by the fluid on that patch?

options.A: Vertically downward, normal to the patch
options.B: Vertically upward, normal to the patch
options.D: In the direction in which the object would move

questions.prompt: Why do the horizontal pressure forces on two equal opposite vertical faces of a symmetric submerged block cancel?

options.A: Fluid pressure is zero on vertical surfaces.
options.B: Each face is at a different depth, so the forces have the same direction.
options.C: Matching areas at matching depths experience equal forces in opposite directions.
options.D: The upward pressure force removes both horizontal forces.

questions.prompt: A submerged cuboid has equal horizontal top and bottom areas. Which statement correctly explains the vertical resultant of the fluid forces?

options.A: The top force is larger because the top is nearer the surface, so the resultant is downward.
options.B: The bottom force is larger because the bottom is deeper, so the resultant is upward.
options.C: The top and bottom forces are equal because their areas are equal, so the resultant is zero.
options.D: Only the side forces contribute, so the resultant is upward.

questions.prompt: A sealed rectangular electronics case is held fully submerged in still water. Its horizontal top and bottom faces have equal area. A cross-section of the case is shown.

figure.purpose: Assess pressure-force directions, relative magnitudes and sideways cancellation without revealing the resultant.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white 3:2 line diagram of a rectangular electronics case fully below a horizontal water surface. Label only top face, bottom face and two side faces. Mark two horizontal depth lines h_top and h_bottom. Include blank arrow boxes outside the four faces for the learner to describe, with no force arrows, relative magnitudes or resultant shown.
figure.alt_text: A rectangular electronics case is fully submerged with labelled top, bottom and side faces at two marked depths.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: State the directions of the water forces on the top and bottom faces.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why the two opposite side faces do not produce a horizontal resultant.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: State the direction of the resultant fluid force and name this force.

questions.prompt: A rectangular marker has horizontal top and bottom faces of equal area 0.024 m². It is fully immersed in a liquid of density 850 kg m⁻³. The vertical separation of the faces is 0.18 m. Take g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Calculate the pressure difference between the bottom and top faces.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Calculate the difference between the pressure forces on these faces.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Explain why your answer to (b) acts upward.

questions.prompt: A closed hollow instrument has a horizontal top plate of area 0.030 m² and a horizontal bottom plate of area 0.018 m². The side walls slope symmetrically. The instrument is fully submerged in water of density 1000 kg m⁻³. The top plate is 0.40 m below the surface and the bottom plate is 0.65 m below the surface. Atmospheric pressure acts equally through the water and need not be included. Take g = 9.81 N kg⁻¹.

figure.purpose: Assess a mixed hydrostatic and pressure-force argument for a symmetric unequal-area body without using Archimedes' principle.
figure.brief: Original black-and-white 3:2 line diagram of a symmetric tapered hollow instrument fully under a flat water surface. Draw a wider horizontal top plate labelled 0.030 m² at depth 0.40 m, a narrower horizontal bottom plate labelled 0.018 m² at depth 0.65 m and two matching sloping side walls. Show depth brackets only. Do not draw pressure arrows, components, a resultant or displaced volume.
figure.alt_text: A symmetric tapered instrument has unequal horizontal top and bottom plates at depths 0.40 metre and 0.65 metre.

parts.label: (a)
parts.prompt: Use the two stated depths to calculate the hydrostatic pressure difference between the levels of the plates.

parts.label: (b)
parts.prompt: Explain why multiplying the pressure difference from (a) by either plate area alone does not give the complete upthrust on this tapered instrument.

parts.label: (c)
parts.prompt: Describe how the pressure forces on the two matching sloping side walls combine. Refer separately to their horizontal and vertical components.

parts.label: (d)
parts.prompt: Use the pressure-force model to explain why the resultant force exerted by the water on the whole instrument is upward.
